newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Danu, Finance One merger said shaky-papers.
newsitem.headline: Thai Danu, Finance One merger said shaky-papers.

text.p: The biggest merger of Thai financial institutions, between Thai Danu Bank Plc and Finance One Plc, is in danger of collapsing, local newspapers reported on Thursday.
The Nation newspaper said the Bank of Thailand was lobbying to prevent a collapse of the merger between medium-sized Thai Danu and Thailand's largest finance firm.
Officials from the companies and the central bank were not available for comment on Thursday, which was a holiday.
The newspaper cited investment banking sources close to the deal who said Thai Danu decided to walk away from the merger due to various problems with Finance One.
Business Day newspaper cited a source at Thai Danu who said the bank was still proceeding with merger steps and the process was ongoing.
The two companies signed a deal to merge and create a new entity in March.
Analysts had said that Finance One sought the merger because it faced liquidity problems which emerged amid a major shakeup of Thailand's troubled finance sector.
Thai Danu said earlier this month it would absorb about six billion baht worth of Finance One's outstanding 21 billion baht ($807.7 million) in property loans when the companies merge.
Finance One has a total of 66 billion baht in outstanding loans.
The due diligence process of assessing the two companies' assets for share swapping purposes was due to take 45 days from the March 14 signing of the initial merger agreement. ($1 = 26 baht)
